subject: Order Form: Rolling Upgrade Windows and Pooled Credit Proposal
messages:
From: Jordan Myers <jordan.myers@scaleup.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+contracts@scaleup.ai
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Rolling upgrades & compensation for partial outages during cutover

Connor — thanks again for the demo last week. We are close to sign but Procurement flagged the rolling upgrade language in the Order Form. Two asks: one, we run large rolling kernel upgrades that can cause short service interruptions (usually 1–3m per shard) during the maintenance window; second, our Ops team wants a predictable credit model that aggregates small interruptions (so we don’t have to file a claim for every 30s hiccup).

Can you propose order form language that: 1) defines what counts as a rolling-upgrade event vs force outage, 2) offers a pooled-credit approach (e.g., accumulate minutes of downtime over a billing period then apply a single credit), and 3) clarifies blackout times (we are on PST).

I attached our standard maintenance calendar for distro. Happy to take a quick call if easier.

—Jordan
Jordan Myers
Director, Platform Ops | ScaleUp AI

Subject: Re: Rolling upgrades & compensation for partial outages during cutover

Jordan — thanks for the clear asks. High-level response below and I attached a short draft you can drop into the Order Form ("pooled-credit-draft.txt").

Proposed approach (summary):
- Definition: "Rolling Upgrade Event" = planned maintenance where Redwood schedules incremental node-level upgrades that may cause transient unavailability on affected shards for up to 5 minutes per shard. Anything beyond 5 minutes or any unplanned interruption is treated as an Incident for SLA calculation.
- Pooled credits: Redwood will accumulate total minutes of unavailability attributed to Rolling Upgrade Events within a given billing month. If accumulated minutes exceed 60 minutes in a month, customer is eligible for a pooled service credit equal to X% of monthly fees (schema in draft).
- Blackouts: Standard maintenance window for planned rolling upgrades is 01:00–05:00 PT. Customer-specified blackout windows (regular business hours) will take precedence; Redwood will not schedule rolling upgrades during those windows without explicit written consent.

Next steps: 1) Legal review of the draft clause (looping Karthik). 2) Ops confirmation on the 5-minute per-shard threshold (looping Marissa). 3) We can surface a numeric credit cap and formula once we confirm optics for pooled-credit threshold.

If you prefer, we can mark this as an appendix to the Order Form rather than changing the MSA. Appendix will be easier to iterate in procurement.

Attachment: pooled-credit-draft.txt (plain text stub)

Looping in operational detail from the runtime side. A few practical notes that should inform contract wording:

- Typical transient KV-cache invalidation or connection drain during a shard upgrade can cause client errors for up to 180s in stress cases; median is closer to 45–90s.
- We currently have automation that retries on transient 5xx and will surface a "grace" window where the platform does not count retries as downtime for internal metrics, but customers often see brief elevated error rates.
- Suggest tightening the per-shard threshold to "up to 3 minutes under normal conditions, up to 5 minutes in edge cases" and include an explicit metric/trace-based attribution requirement (Redwood traces must show upgrade marker + elevated error window) to qualify minutes for the pooled bucket. This prevents unrelated infra incidents from being counted toward rolling-upgrade minutes.

Happy to run a short sync between ScaleUp infra and our SREs if you want traces from prior upgrades to calibrate the numbers.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Rolling upgrades & compensation for partial outages during cutover

Jordan — thanks for raising this. From legal: attached is a redline we would prefer to push into the Order Form as an appendix. Key changes we propose:

- Narrow the definition: require Redwood upgrade markers in trace logs plus a correlating increase in error-rate for a contiguous window to qualify; this prevents aggregated credits for unrelated outages.
- Cap the pooled credit: maximum 10% of monthly fees per billing period and a per-event cap equal to 25% of the available pooled credit.
- Exclude previously scheduled customer blackout overrides (we will not schedule by default, but if customer requests out-of-window upgrade the event is not eligible).
- Provide a "measurement and claim" process: customer must open a ticket within 14 days of the billing period close with traces and request; Redwood will validate within 7 business days.

If ScaleUp is comfortable with the appendix approach and the caps above, we can update the Order Form and route through Procurement. If you need looser caps, note that will require an uplift in price for Dedicated capacity or a different SLA tier.

Looping Lauren for commercial approval on the caps and whether we should offer a one-time goodwill credit to keep momentum.

—Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
